topic: OpenCost statistical analysis and private feedback
scope: Agent evaluation, cost-quality tradeoffs, clustered observations, partial pooling, missingness, task-mixture comparison, selection bias, multiple testing, uncertainty and recommendation validation

searchNotes.inclusion: Original paper, author-hosted manuscript, publisher abstract, official institutional repository, or official NIST method page; direct applicability to the current OpenCost feedback estimand
searchNotes.exclusion: Search-only secondary commentary, unverified leaderboard claims, guessed paper identity, unrelated papers, and model performance numbers not required for algorithm design
searchNotes.dataAccess: Only public literature and local source code were read; no user logs, credentials, production database, or project upload was used.
searchNotes.limitation: No exhaustive database export, citation-network saturation, dual screening, formal risk-of-bias assessment, or all-paper full-text review was performed. Publication years were taken from the original work rather than search engine crawl or online-migration dates.

readingLevels.selected_full_text: Original full text was opened and relevant sections/formulas were read; not a claim that every page or proof was audited.
readingLevels.primary_abstract: Original author/publisher abstract and metadata were read.
readingLevels.primary_search_abstract: Search returned the publisher's abstract and metadata; a subsequent direct open failed. No full-text reading claimed.
readingLevels.official_method_full: Relevant official method page, formula and assumptions were read.
readingLevels.author_book_page_and_primary_excerpt: Author book page was read and an author-hosted chapter excerpt was returned by search; full book download via browser failed.

sources.title: AI Agents That Matter
sectionsRead: Appendix B fixed and variable costs
supports: Joint cost and success evaluation
Total agent cost includes retries and fixed/variable components
Preserve tokens and historical price for separate repricing
Distinguish model science from downstream procurement
sources.migrationLimit: Its benchmark experiments and Pareto mixtures are not calibrated real-work difficulty or proof of savings in OpenCost.

sources.title: Holistic Evaluation of Language Models
sectionsRead: Abstract and TMLR 2023 publication metadata; arXiv v2
supports: Scenario taxonomy
Multiple metrics and explicit missing scenario coverage
Standardized comparison conditions
sources.migrationLimit: Does not provide a universal scalar difficulty score; prompt and completion publication is incompatible with the OpenCost no-content-upload goal.

sources.title: AgentBench: Evaluating LLMs as Agents
sectionsRead: Abstract; ICLR 2024 metadata; arXiv v3 revised 2025-10-04
supports: Interactive environments differ
Long-term reasoning, decision and instruction-following failure dimensions
sources.migrationLimit: Benchmark environment scores cannot be assigned to unrelated private work without domain-specific validation.

sources.title: τ-bench: A Benchmark for Tool-Agent-User Interaction in Real-World Domains
sectionsRead: Pass^k metric and unbiased combination formulas
supports: Repeated reliability differs from best-of-k success
Same-task n trials and c successes are required
Trial comparability and i.i.d. assumptions are explicit
sources.migrationLimit: Do not treat adaptive real-world retries as independent trials or report completion^k as measured pass^k.

sources.title: A Practitioner's Guide to Cluster-Robust Inference
sectionsRead: VI.C pairs cluster bootstrap and caution
supports: Resample source clusters rather than tasks
Correlated tasks do not supply independent precision
Few or highly unequal clusters can invalidate naive intervals
Do not discard undefined bootstrap replicates
sources.migrationLimit: Regression guidance does not itself validate a percentile interval for a cost/success ratio; dedicated operating-characteristic checks are needed.

sources.title: Cluster-Robust Inference: A Guide to Empirical Practice
supports: Cluster count alone is not sufficient
Report concentration, heterogeneity and influence
Known clustering assignment and cross-cluster assumptions matter
sources.migrationLimit: Inverse source concentration is a descriptive measure, not the paper's coefficient-specific effective cluster count.

sources.title: Why We (Usually) Don't Have to Worry About Multiple Comparisons
supports: Partial pooling for related sparse groups
Shrinkage must follow an explicit hierarchical model
sources.migrationLimit: Does not license ignoring multiplicity in arbitrary dashboards; no fixed pseudo-count can replace model diagnostics or remove selection bias.

sources.title: Inference and Missing Data
sectionsRead: Publisher abstract and bibliographic metadata in search result
supports: Ignoring the missingness process requires assumptions
Observed-case data cannot automatically stand for all tasks
sources.accessLimit: Direct open failed; no full-text reading claimed.
sources.migrationLimit: The abstract does not justify identifying a missingness mechanism from the uploaded summaries.

sources.title: The Interpretation of Interaction in Contingency Tables
sectionsRead: Publisher summary and original issue metadata
supports: Aggregated comparisons require care about table structure and task mix
sources.accessLimit: Direct open later failed; no full-text reading claimed. Publisher's online migration date is not the 1951 publication year.
sources.migrationLimit: Task-mix standardization is an OpenCost adaptation, not a causal guarantee from this paper.

sources.title: Controlling the False Discovery Rate: A Practical and Powerful Approach to Multiple Testing
sectionsRead: Original PDF found but extraction returned zero text lines; procedure also read in SF11
supports: FDR differs from familywise error
Original guarantee assumes independent test statistics
sources.migrationLimit: Do not apply multiplicity correction to invalid p-values or to a selectively reported subset of a larger family.

sources.title: The Control of the False Discovery Rate in Multiple Testing under Dependency
sectionsRead: PRDS definition and results for other dependencies
supports: BH has dependency conditions
A harmonic correction addresses arbitrary dependency for valid tests
Predefine the family of comparisons
sources.accessLimit: Publisher endpoint returned no usable body; author-hosted original PDF was used.
sources.migrationLimit: Does not solve confounding, adaptively chosen hypotheses, or invalid unit-of-analysis assumptions.

sources.title: On Over-fitting in Model Selection and Subsequent Selection Bias in Performance Evaluation
sectionsRead: Model-selection variance and nested validation discussion
supports: Picking the observed minimum introduces optimistic selection bias
Separate candidate selection from held-out evaluation
sources.migrationLimit: A historical cheapest-Harness display can remain descriptive; future savings need additional held-out evidence.

sources.title: Statistical Comparisons of Classifiers over Multiple Data Sets
sectionsRead: Section 3 independent datasets as sample units
Friedman test and repeated dependent samples caveats
supports: The independent unit is not every repeated execution
Paired comparisons require genuinely paired task evaluation
sources.migrationLimit: Unpaired community uploads cannot be turned into a matched benchmark by matching a coarse task label.

sources.title: Strictly Proper Scoring Rules, Prediction, and Estimation
supports: Backtest predicted probabilities with proper scores
Evaluate prediction intervals by both width and coverage
Do not reward arbitrarily wide intervals
sources.migrationLimit: A proper score evaluates forecasts; it is not a universal task-difficulty or output-quality score.

sources.title: Causal Inference: What If
supports: Measured-condition standardization and causal identification are different requirements
Conditionally similar records do not establish causal savings
sources.accessLimit: Author page points to changing book revisions. Latest linked PDF could not be read through browser; no full-book reading or latest-revision proof claimed.
sources.migrationLimit: OpenCost lacks random assignment, full confounders and exchangeability evidence; all current recommendations remain observational.

sources.title: NIST/SEMATECH e-Handbook: 7.2.4.1 Confidence Intervals
sectionsRead: Exact binomial alternative and terminology note
supports: Closed-form bounded binomial interval
Avoid Wald intervals with impossible limits
sources.migrationLimit: A binomial interval cannot account for unknown source/task dependence or selective upload.

sources.title: NIST/SEMATECH e-Handbook: How Can I Predict the Value and Estimate the Uncertainty of a Single Response?
sectionsRead: Prediction interval variance formula and coverage factor
supports: Future payment intervals need future-process variation in addition to parameter error
Distinguish confidence, prediction and observed ranges
sources.migrationLimit: The regression-normal formula is not directly applicable to zero-inflated skewed task costs; definition transfers, not the unvalidated numeric formula.

sources.title: Nonparametric Estimation from Incomplete Observations
sectionsRead: Publisher abstract and original publication metadata
supports: Incomplete follow-up differs from an observed terminal failure
Record observation cutoffs and censoring reasons before time-to-event analysis
sources.accessLimit: Direct open failed; no full-text reading claimed.
sources.migrationLimit: Task abandonment/failure can be competing outcomes; do not assume independent censoring or deploy Kaplan-Meier directly from current status counts.
